footnotes.text: 1. Regardless of individual course grades, students must maintain a minimum 2.000 cumulative GPA.

evidence.quote: 1. Regardless of individual course grades, students must maintain a minimum 2.000 cumulative GPA.

footnotes.text: 2. Some colleges require a minimum GPA for major courses. Courses indicated in this column are included in the major GPA for this program of study.

evidence.quote: 2. Some colleges require a minimum GPA for major courses. Courses indicated in this column are included in the major GPA for this program of study.

footnotes.text: 3. Students in the College of Arts and Sciences are required to demonstrate proficiency in one foreign language equivalent to the 122 course through course credit or the corresponding foreign language placement score.

evidence.quote: 3. Students in the College of Arts and Sciences are required to demonstrate proficiency in one foreign language equivalent to the 122 course through course credit or the corresponding foreign language placement score.

footnotes.text: 4. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

evidence.quote: 4. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

footnotes.text: 5. The College of Arts and Sciences requires one U.S. History and one non-U.S. History course, both of which must be chosen from the approved Carolina Core GHS courses. Whichever is not fulfilled through the Carolina Core GHS requirement must be fulfilled through this college requirement.

evidence.quote: 5. The College of Arts and Sciences requires one U.S. History and one non-U.S. History course, both of which must be chosen from the approved Carolina Core GHS courses. Whichever is not fulfilled through the Carolina Core GHS requirement must be fulfilled through this college requirement.

footnotes.text: 6. The cognate is intended to support the course work in the major. The cognate must consist of twelve hours of courses at the advanced level, outside of, but related to the major. In place of the cognate, a student may choose a minor consisting of at least 18 credit hours of courses concentrated in one area that follow a structured sequence. Students completing the Secondary Education English concentration must also complete an Education coursework component that may fulfill the cognate requirement.

footnotes.text: 7. English Major courses, equaling 33 hours, must be comprised of the following: • One course (3 hours) in pre-1800 Literature • One course (3 hours) in post-1800 Literature • ENGL 450 (3 hours) • ENGL 432 (3 hours) • ENGL 437 (3 hours) • ENGL 460 (3 hours) • ENGL elective (3 hours) 300-level or above • English Language (3 hours): ENGL 389, 453 • Theory and Criticism (3 hours): ENGL 388, 440, 449 • African American Literature (3 hours): ENGL 428A, 428B, 430 • Writing or Rhetoric (3 hours): ENGL 360, 387, 461, 462, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468, 469, 470, 471, 472, 485, 486 • The major in English requires a diversity course (0-3 hours), which may also serve as a pre- or post-1800 literature course or an elective. Students who do not meet this Diversity Requirement through another major requirement must take a course in addition to the m ajor requirements. For a list of courses fulfilling the pre-1800 and post-1800 Literature requirements, and the Diversity Requirement, please visit the Bulletin.
